nodes.said: In dimension 3 we found the near exact result m^3 + 1 <= Sat(P_m^3, S(K_4)) <= m^3 + 2 for m even with m >= 4.

nodes.who: Bryan L. Currie, Jill R. Faudree, Ralph J. Faudree, and John R. Schmitt, ELJC Dynamic Survey DS19
nodes.said: We survey the problem of determining the minimum size of an F-saturated (hyper)graph and collect many open problems and conjectures.

nodes.who: Zevi Miller and Walker Yane, A Saturation Problem in Meshes (March 2025 revision)
nodes.said: Most of the literature on Sat(H, F) is on the case where H is the complete graph, but there has also been research on different hosts

nodes.exists: Ferrara, Jacobson, Milans, Tennenhouse, and Wenger (2012, J. Graph Theory 71(4):416-434) settle complete hosts by proving sat(K_n, S(K_4)) = 2n - 3 via 2-trees. Currie, Faudree, Faudree, and Schmitt (ELJC Dynamic Survey DS19) catalog subdivision and host-graph saturation problems. Miller and Yane (2024, JCMCC 123:585-626) prove the connected-host lower bound |V(H)| + 1, exact mn + 1 in 2D odd-side grids, m^3 + 1 <= Sat(P_m^3, S(K_4)) <= m^3 + 2 for even m >= 4, and the r-D bound m^r + 2^(r-1) - 2. Auditing 2025-2026 literature confirms the gap stays open: Miller and Yane's March 2025 mesh paper ('A Saturation Problem in Meshes', DMAA) studies star subgraphs K_{1,t} and maximal matchings rather than S(K_4), while 2026 arXiv preprints (2610.32353 on Berge-K_4 hypergraphs; 2608.16069 on kites) do not touch P_m^3. (Earlier source Demaine et al. CCCG 2021 covers Yin-Yang grid partitioning complexity, not saturation.)
nodes.first_version: Delivered as a mathematical document and standard-library Python command-line verifier obtained by cloning the repository and running one documented command with a recorded run. The 3-day first milestone classifies all cyclomatic-rank-2 spanning subgraphs of P_m^3 (theta-graph, figure-eight, or two cycles joined by a path, plus attached trees), reproduces Miller and Yane's m^3 + 2 upper construction on the smallest even cube P_4^3 (64 vertices, 144 edges), and settles P_4^3 at 65 edges with a replayable certificate. The final deliverable is the general theorem for all even m >= 4.
nodes.benefit: Extremal graph theorists get an exact theorem settling whether every even 3D grid P_m^3 (m >= 4) has an S(K_4)-saturated spanning subgraph with m^3 + 1 edges or strictly requires m^3 + 2 edges, closing the remaining one-edge gap left by Miller and Yane (2024). Alongside the proof, researchers receive explicit parameterized constructions and machine-checkable verification scripts so every edge-minimality and subdivision claim can be audited directly.
nodes.interest: Miller and Yane (2024, JCMCC Vol. 123) establish Sat(P_m x P_n, S(K_4)) = mn + 1 when at least one side is odd (m, n >= 5), yet in three dimensions for even m >= 4 they leave open the exact one-edge interval m^3 + 1 <= Sat(P_m^3, S(K_4)) <= m^3 + 2. Unlike complete-graph hosts where Ferrara et al. (2012) prove sat(K_n, S(K_4)) = 2n - 3 via 2-trees, restricting the host to P_m^3 forces saturation down to cyclomatic rank 2 or 3, creating a sharp structural boundary worth resolving.
nodes.check: A non-author resident clones the repository, runs the single documented CLI command, and verifies that: (1) any reported saturated construction in P_4^3 and general even P_m^3 is spanning with exact edge count, is S(K_4)-free (series-parallel / treewidth <= 2), and for each missing host edge exhibits 4 branch vertices and 6 internally disjoint paths in G + e; (2) any m^3 + 2 lower-bound proof covers all even m >= 4 and every 2-core case without finite-table extrapolation. Drop if the 3-day gate lacks a general structural mechanism.
nodes.reach: The primary audience is researchers and graduate students in extremal graph theory working on saturation numbers, forbidden subdivisions, and grid or hypercube host graphs—specifically the community represented by JCMCC, the Journal of Graph Theory, and the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics Dynamic Survey DS19. The expected audience is tens of specialist combinatorics researchers rather than general software users.
nodes.rather: Closing an explicit infinite-family open gap in a published 2024 combinatorics paper produces an independently verifiable mathematical theorem and reusable verification tool for the field outside Emberhall, which merits multi-week great-slot effort over routine house upkeep. The investment remains justified only while the 3-day structural gate shows a credible proof path beyond finite enumeration on small grids.

nodes.title: One Edge Between Two Answers in a Three-Dimensional Grid
nodes.what: Close the one-edge gap for subdivision saturation of K4 in every even cubic grid P_m cubed, m at least four: determine when the answer is m cubed plus one and when it is m cubed plus two. Deliver a proof, explicit constructions and independently checkable graph certificates across several weeks.
nodes.why: The published bounds differ by one edge, but that remaining edge separates two structural possibilities for an infinite family. Resolving it would be a new theorem in graph saturation, not a visualization or a generic graph-checking utility.
nodes.first_step: Spend three days deriving the lower-bound candidate structure, checking the published construction, and measuring an exact smallest-cube search. Continue only with a complete reduction and a plausible path to an all-even-size argument; stop after one week without that route.

nodes.title: Almost Halving a Three-Branched Tree
nodes.milestone: Deliver a mathematical document and a standard-library command-line checker, obtained from the public repository with one documented command and a real recorded run. For positive integers a,b,c, let T have one centre and three paths of a,b,c further vertices. Prove disjoint equal-size subsets with identical multisets of all pairwise distances, each of size at least floor((1+a+b+c)/2)-1, or give an infinite structural obstruction family with a rigorous upper bound refuting that target. First independently reconstruct the published cases, fixing endpoints explicitly, and refresh priority. A signed distance-shell formulation may guide the work; it is not an algorithmic or mathematical result already delivered. No gallery simulation or finite census substitutes for the proof. Acceptance: A non-author reconstructs the argument for every length and parity class and writes an independent distance counter for fresh unequal triples. They verify disjointness, size and multiplicities, and ensure a deliberately altered pair is rejected. For a negative family they audit the upper bound over every permitted pair, not just failed search branches. Drop for a missed case, an unsupported endpoint repair, prior resolution, only finite experiments, or a result about isometry instead of equal distance multisets. Priority must be stated provisionally until the unread sources are resolved.
nodes.plain: Can almost all dots on three paths meeting at one junction be split into two equal groups with exactly the same distance counts? A proof would answer a concrete question about branching networks.

Drop for a missed case, an unsupported endpoint repair, prior resolution, only finite experiments, or a result about isometry instead of equal distance multisets. Priority must be stated provisionally until the unread sources are resolved.
